title: Evals Are Broken, Use Them Anyway — Ara Khan, Cline
talk_summary: Ara Khan argues evals are neither gospel nor useless: ignore vendor benchmark numbers, use fresh/precise task suites, and treat evals as an engineering hill-climbing loop. He describes Cline's use of Terminal Bench (89 real-world agent tasks) run in parallel isolated VMs via Harbor, then triaging failure traces to find small harness levers (CPU/memory, timeouts, thinking behavior, per-model prompting).

takeaways.technique: Hill-climb on a real-task eval suite
takeaways.what_they_do: Run a fixed suite of realistic agent tasks, score it, then iterate on the harness and re-score, separating obvious bugs (zone 1), nuanced per-model tuning (zone 2), and overfitting (zone 3).
takeaways.evidence_quote: find a benchmark and like like build the eval and just like hill climb on it
takeaways.numbers: Cline started at 43% on Terminal Bench; improved via CPU/memory, timeouts, thinking behavior

takeaways.what_they_do: After an eval run, spawn an agent that reads the full traces of failed tasks and categorizes why each failed (missing tool, broken retry, timeout), yielding concrete levers.
takeaways.evidence_quote: run like uh another agent which goes through the traces of all the failures

takeaways.what_they_do: Define each eval task with its own Linux VM spec (RAM/CPU) and run all tasks in parallel on remote infra so wall-clock equals the slowest task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: isolate those environments and then run those 89 tasks in parallel on infrastructure
takeaways.numbers: 89 tasks; slowest task is the limiting factor

takeaways.what_they_do: Recognize that prompting techniques that work for one model family fail for another, and tune prompts/harness per family rather than assuming a good model will just work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: certain prompt engineering techniques that apply to entropic model families that just straight up would not apply to Codex model family

takeaways.technique: Distrust vendor benchmark numbers; wait for settling
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat published model scores as approximations and delay adopting new models a couple weeks until independent evidence accumulates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: whenever a model apps comes out with like a number, just don't believe them

takeaways.what_they_do: Experiment with asking the model to think more or less; more thinking sometimes degrades output by looping.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Sometimes asking model to think more actually interferes with the quality of the response
